schema.identity: actorDefinitionId + definitionVersion; canonical assetId + exact shipped assetVersion; no model URL/base64 inside definitions
schema.animation: Definition overrides merge into an actor-local copy of the existing manifest mapping; every required mapped clip must exist before cloning. Shared source config is never changed. The fixed authored Mourning sampler rejects conflicting remaps explicitly.
schema.style: Existing monster-toon, character-outline and character-surface/internal-line paths and scene settings; no new visual variant or quality reduction
schema.bounds: Independent posed mesh bounds; existing render-range padding; collider comes from current encounter constants
schema.behaviorMovementHp: Registered HP is applied to each fresh brain's hp/maxHp; collider radius/stopDistance/separationRadius are applied at construction and activation. Built-in values remain unchanged. Movement selects the exact existing encounter profile; conflicting overrides reject explicitly rather than altering root travel/attack timing or being ignored. Optional maxHp must equal hp for the supported full-health spawn profile.
schema.spawn: Development-only group, count/interval data, allowed maps, current navigation free-space test, player safety distance and explicit overlap rejection
schema.respawn: Development scenario data uses8game-time seconds; pause while game paused/map inactive. NPC representative disables respawn. This does not add automatic enemies/rewards to normal maps.
schema.population: Per-definition maxPooled, conservative estimatedBytes reservation and30s idleSeconds; total/type/memory/preparation caps are owned by ActorPopulation
schema.lod: Current full-quality path with no reduced existing LOD; data includes a future per-definition screen-coverage policy slot
schema.references: Existing drop/quest/NPC handler identifiers only; no new story, reward amounts or raw assets

api.factoryReturn: create(definitionOrId,{generation,isCurrent,preparation}) -> adapter; await-compatible synchronous construction. create.inspect() reports actor/library keys/model load count; create.dispose() returns pending owned cleanup.
api.libraryOverride: libraryFactory(scene,assetId,assetVersion) returns library or {library,owned:false}; owned:false explicitly keeps caller-owned source containers/materials alive
api.validationResult: {valid:true,position} or {valid:false,reason}; no silent relocation or count reduction
api.lifetimeToken: create context.isCurrent must describe the record/map generation lifetime; per-operation options.isCurrent and preparation describe only the current prepare/activate operation. ActorPopulation owns the separate tokens.
api.snapshot: {active,dead,dying,corpseGone,combat,incoming,projectile,questRelevant,rewardGranted,position,life,decisionCount}; dying follows authored death pose completion, leaving observable held/fading corpse state
api.activity: NPC dialogue references do not imply always-urgent decisions. spawnContext.questRelevant or live getActivity result can elevate actual tracked/active quest, incoming or projectile semantics; interaction remains callable independently.

combatIntegration.pipelineOwner: Existing BossBattle alone updates combat actors, separates bodies, reconciles navigation, prepares poses and processes strike/contact order. Combat adapter.update is intentionally a no-op.
combatIntegration.publication: Activation adds its exact encounter once to battle.encounters. Hide removes only that encounter. Combat construction/disposal registers/unregisters battle.developmentPool; root extends existing allPooled to retain global gate/reset/style behavior without changing production indexed pools.
combatIntegration.playerState: All actors share the existing battle.combat. Adapter reset/hide never resets player HP, potions, invulnerability, another enemy's grab or the global combat clock.
combatIntegration.npc: Representative stays outside battle.encounters/developmentPool and never calls the hostile encounter update. It keeps prepared visual updates; its harmless decision method can be distance-scheduled. interact delegates existing guard ID/actor position/range to root's readiness/combat/distance/LOS guard, then existing ChapterQuests.talk.
combatIntegration.manualDeath: defeat() asks the existing brain.hit for a lethal heavy hit and respects its defense acceptance. Normal death/fade/corpse and callback paths perform the rest; no UI writes HP directly.
combatIntegration.rewards: onDefeat is acknowledged at most once per life. Gameplay callback requires explicit rewardsEnabled=true; the development UI leaves it false, so load/death/respawn demonstrations cannot farm real gold or quest progress. No alternate reward engine exists.

warmReuse.assetCreation: BossModelLibrary.load is reused per assetId@version, but every pooled actor invokes existing instantiateBossModel(container) directly. This shares geometry/material/texture sources and clones independent skeletons, animation targets and morph managers. It never uses the special single-resident Elena/Mourning adoption branch.
warmReuse.firstPreparation: Existing prepareHidden, createBossPreparation step budget, toon/internal-line/outline, bounds proof and shader preparation paths remain authoritative. Clone expansion is one existing preparation.step; no second scheduler was added.
warmReuse.optInSummon: BossEncounter.summon({reuseAnimator:true}) resets the already prepared animator via CharacterAnimator.resetForReuse or MourningElenaAnimator's existing reset, then uses the unchanged brain/summon/death reset path.
warmReuse.optInHideDeath: Only encounters tagged retainAnimatorForPool skip animator disposal on hide/corpse completion. Default production summon/hide/death disposal remains unchanged.
warmReuse.bindingReuse: CharacterAnimator.retainBindings keeps previously used paused native clip animatables at weight0 instead of stop/delete. resetForReuse clears playback/action/blend/weight state; switching back to a known clip reuses its exact native binding. Clip states are bounded by the actor's existing manifest, not every future model.
warmReuse.zeroWeightFix: Retained fade completion explicitly sets the native group's weight to0 before skipping it, preventing the previous action from contributing residual pose. A native-animation regression compares the result with the default stop/delete path.
warmReuse.poolReset: Hide/reset clear hit flash, mesh visibility, targets/player refs, pending events, grab/gate, knockback/reaction, route/contact/reposition caches, telegraph/contact/slam resources, counters, HP/death/playback and per-life reward acknowledgement before the next activation. The adapter owns no sound objects, timers or per-frame observers; onActorHide permits root-owned audio cleanup.

ownership.libraryCaps: Entry reference count tracks adapters. Final adapter eviction removes only the exact assetId@version entry and releases its owned source container/derived toon materials; a later spawn is deliberately cold after idle eviction. Warm respawn before eviction keeps the entry. Sources cannot accumulate uncharged across arbitrary definition/version visits.
ownership.scopedLoader: Default dev library opts into new BossModelLibrary(scene,id,{scoped:true}); root owns the bounded/cancellable loader extension. Final owned entry calls library.dispose immediately before awaiting pending completion. Existing production library default and borrowed owned:false libraries remain untouched.
ownership.retirementAccounting: adapter.dispose returns completion of its existing acquisition/warm/source cleanup promises. ActorPopulation keeps retiring slots/estimated memory charged until actual cleanup settles, preventing repeated cancelled map jobs from escaping caps.
ownership.perActorDisposal: Only owned cloned animation groups, actor/child nodes, skeletons and independent morph managers, warning/contact/spell auxiliaries are disposed. Shared source geometry/material/textures remain while another clone/library owns them.
ownership.sceneOwned: Existing scene-shared outline material, scene render ordering and inactive fog sampler remain owned by the original scene modules; the adapter does not dispose another actor's scene-wide resources.
ownership.lateResults: Generation and scene/map identity are checked before clone/activation. Late cancelled acquisitions are cleaned through exact owned asset sets and never published as current-map actors.

Map/navigation/occupancy/player safety failures are rejected explicitly without relocating the input position.
Two real Babylon cloned skeleton/animation-target instances are independent while sharing geometry/material; one source load serves them.
Five warm lives preserve exact animator/skeleton/geometry/material identities and issue zero new AnimationGroup.start calls for the prepared idle clip; scene resource counts remain fixed.
Retained crossfade writes native weight0; after native frame flush its sampled pose matches the ordinary stop/delete path.
Corpse completion retains the opted-in animator; defeat callback occurs once per life and next life resets acknowledgement.
NPC remains outside battle, delegates guard interaction and does not manufacture rewards.
Last-clone disposal releases owned source only once, preserves another clone and all borrowed sources, and removes library accounting.
Map-generation change during a delayed source load prevents clone creation/publication and releases retirement cleanup.
An unflagged BossEncounter still disposes/recreates on summon and disposes on hide in the existing order.

limitations: No browser automation, real GPU pixels, mobile FPS/temperature/input-latency or20actors-at60FPS guarantee.
Triangle totals distinguish indexed triangulated geometry and base/outline/shadow submission estimates; an estimate is not measured GPU frame cost.
Estimated memory reservations are conservative development accounting, not a driver memory measurement. Independent verifier reports actual resource counts separately.
New clip activation may establish that clip's binding once when first needed; warm lives retain previously used clips. Pool caps bound retained native clip state.

New movement profiles and remapping the fixed-channel Mourning sampler require an explicit future encounter implementation. Registration currently rejects those unsupported conflicts; it never silently ignores them or changes approved motion timing.
NPC is an explicit development visual representative reusing existing guard interaction; this phase does not author new village dialogue/content.
No normal-play bulk spawn, reward, existing actor LOD or current combat/input order was changed by these definitions/adapters.
Root owns lazy actorLab integration, existing battle loader/allPooled hooks, final release routing and deployment.
